skill.name: gh-fix-ci
skill.description: Inspect GitHub Actions PR checks, pull failing logs, summarize failure context, and implement approved CI fixes with gh.
skill.summary: Inspect GitHub Actions PR failures, summarize logs, plan fixes, and implement approved CI repairs.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick, hardcoded URL, and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown examples in SKILL.md. The main concern is semantic: the skill directs agents to request broad gh scopes and sandbox escalation, so it needs clearer consent and least-privilege guidance.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends escalated GitHub scopes and sandbox permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit user confirmation step before gh auth scope changes or sandbox escalation, and document the minimum required scopes.

remediation.issue: CI logs may include secrets or private repository details.
remediation.suggestion: Instruct assistants to redact tokens, credentialed URLs, and private data before summarizing or sharing logs.

remediation.issue: The referenced helper script is not present in the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Include the script in the package or remove script commands so users do not rely on missing resources.

semantic_findings.title: Elevated GitHub And Sandbox Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks the assistant to use gh with workflow/repo scopes and rerun gh auth status with sandbox_permissions=require_escalated. This can expose GitHub credentials or broaden repository access without a strong consent gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly request escalated GitHub scopes and sandbox permission escalation. The CI context is legitimate, but the privilege increase is real for a community skill.

content.value_statement: Failing pull request checks slow releases when logs are spread across GitHub Actions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through check inspection, log review, planning, and approved fixes.
actual_capabilities: Checks GitHub CLI authentication before running PR inspection steps.
Uses a PR number, PR URL, or current branch to identify the target pull request.
Inspects GitHub Actions check status and separates external providers from in-scope checks.
Fetches failing run metadata and logs with GitHub CLI commands.
Summarizes failing check names, run URLs, missing logs, and useful log snippets.
Requires an approved plan before implementing code changes.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI session with access to the target repository.
Focuses on GitHub Actions; Buildkite and other external providers are out of scope.
The audited package contains only SKILL.md; the referenced helper script was not present.
Cannot guarantee a fix without project tests, repository context, and user approval.

use_cases.title: Triage Pull Request Failures
use_cases.description: Inspect failing GitHub Actions checks, collect the relevant log snippet, and identify the likely failure source.

use_cases.title: Recover Release Branch CI
use_cases.description: Review failing release checks, separate external provider noise, and prepare a focused repair plan.

use_cases.title: Guide Assistant-Based Fixes
use_cases.description: Give an AI coding assistant a structured workflow for CI diagnosis, planning, implementation, and recheck guidance.
use_cases.target_user: Developer using Claude Code or Codex

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Current PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for the current branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci on this repository. Inspect the current branch PR, summarize failing GitHub Actions checks, and propose a fix plan before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Specific PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused triage for a known pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci for PR <number-or-url>. Report failing GitHub Actions checks, include concise log snippets, and mark external checks out of scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A CI Repair
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow after failures are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci to inspect the failing checks, explain the likely cause, draft a minimal fix plan, and wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose And Recheck
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with implementation and verification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-fix-ci on this PR. After I approve the plan, implement the fix, summarize changed files and tests, then suggest the exact CI recheck steps.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to debug the current pull request checks.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the failing workflow, includes a short log excerpt, explains the likely cause, and asks for approval on a fix plan.

output_examples.input: A maintainer provides a PR URL with mixed GitHub Actions and external checks.
output_examples.output: The assistant inspects GitHub Actions checks, labels external checks as out of scope, and shares the relevant details URLs.

output_examples.input: A release engineer approves a proposed CI fix.
output_examples.output: The assistant applies the approved change, summarizes diffs and tests, and recommends rerunning the relevant pull request checks.

best_practices: Confirm GitHub CLI authentication and repository access before inspecting checks.
Review and approve the proposed fix plan before implementation starts.
Keep log snippets short and redact secrets or private repository details.
anti_patterns: Running code changes before the user approves the fix plan.
Treating external providers as in scope after only seeing a details URL.
Sharing full CI logs that may contain tokens or private data.

faq.question: Does this skill fix every CI provider?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on GitHub Actions and reports external provider URLs as out of scope.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on an authenticated gh session with access to the target repository.

faq.question: Will it change code automatically?
faq.answer: It should draft a plan and wait for user approval before making code changes.

faq.question: Can it inspect private repositories?
faq.answer: Only when the local gh session has permission to access that repository.

faq.question: Does the audited package include helper scripts?
faq.answer: No. The audited file set contains SKILL.md only, even though the instructions reference a script.

faq.question: What should users watch for?
faq.answer: Users should review any request for broader GitHub scopes, sandbox escalation, or CI log sharing.
